questions.text: Choose the correct form: She ___ to school every day.
questions.explanation: With third person singular (she/he/it) we add -s: goes.

questions.text: Which word is an adjective?
questions.explanation: 'Beautiful' describes a noun, so it is an adjective.

questions.text: Pick the correct preposition: I'm interested ___ movies.
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'interested in'.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.explanation: The correct structure is 'I am [number] years old'.

questions.text: Which is correct? There ___ a cat and two dogs in the garden.
questions.explanation: When 'there is/are' precedes a list, the verb agrees with the first noun: 'a cat' is singular, so we use 'is'.

title: Travel English
description: Useful phrases and vocabulary for trips (A1-A2)

questions.text: 'Where is the nearest station?' — you want to know...
questions.explanation: You are asking for location or directions to the station.

questions.text: Choose the most polite request:
options: Can I have some water, please?
questions.explanation: 'Can I have…, please?' is the most polite and natural form.

questions.text: A 'boarding pass' is required when you...
questions.explanation: A boarding pass is your ticket to board an aircraft.

questions.text: What does 'departure' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Departure' means the act of leaving a place.

questions.text: Fill in: 'Could you ___ me to the nearest pharmacy?'
options: All of the above are correct
questions.explanation: All three — show, direct, and take — are correct and natural in this context.

questions.text: What is the opposite of 'ancient'?
questions.explanation: 'Modern' means new or recent — the opposite of ancient.

questions.text: Choose the correct word: I need to ___ a dentist appointment.
questions.explanation: We 'make' an appointment, not 'do' it.

questions.text: Which word means 'to look for something'?
questions.explanation: 'Search' means to actively look for something.

questions.text: What does 'affordable' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Affordable' means priced low enough that people can pay for it.

questions.text: Choose the correct collocation: ___ a decision
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is 'make a decision'.

questions.text: What does 'exhausted' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Exhausted' means extremely tired, much stronger than just 'tired'.

title: English Tenses
description: Present and past tenses in action (A2-B1)

questions.text: Which sentence is in the Present Continuous?
questions.explanation: Present Continuous uses 'is/am/are + verb-ing' to describe actions happening now.

questions.text: Fill in: I ___ to Paris twice in my life.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect ('have been') is used for life experiences without a specific time.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: When I ___ a child, I loved cartoons.
questions.explanation: Past Simple 'was' is used for states in the past.

questions.text: Which is correct? She ___ her homework already.
questions.explanation: 'Already' with Present Perfect: 'has finished' shows the action is complete before now.

questions.text: Fill in: I ___ dinner when he called.
questions.explanation: Past Continuous 'was cooking' shows an ongoing action interrupted by another ('he called').

title: Phrasal Verbs
description: Essential phrasal verbs for natural speech (B1)

questions.text: 'Give up' means:
questions.explanation: 'Give up' means to stop trying or to quit.

questions.text: 'Get over' something means:
questions.explanation: 'Get over' means to recover from something, like an illness or a difficult experience.

questions.text: Choose the correct phrasal verb: 'Can you ___ this form, please?' (complete it)
options: Both A and C are correct
questions.explanation: Both 'fill in' and 'fill out' mean to complete a form. Both are correct.

questions.text: 'Look forward to' means:
options: to be excited about something in the future
questions.explanation: 'Look forward to' means to feel excited and positive about something coming soon.

questions.text: Fill in: 'The meeting was ___ due to bad weather.' (cancelled/postponed)
questions.explanation: 'Call off' means to cancel an event.

questions.text: What does 'deadline' mean?
options: the last date to complete a task
questions.explanation: A 'deadline' is the final date or time by which work must be completed.

questions.text: Which phrase means 'to start a discussion'?
questions.explanation: 'Kick off' means to start something, especially a meeting or project.

questions.text: What does 'proactive' mean?
options: acting in advance to prevent problems
questions.explanation: Being 'proactive' means taking action before problems happen, not waiting.

questions.text: Choose the most professional phrase for ending an email:
questions.explanation: 'Kind regards' is a standard, professional email sign-off.

questions.text: 'Bottom line' in business means:
options: the net profit or the key conclusion
questions.explanation: 'Bottom line' refers to net profit on financial statements, or informally, the most important point.

title: Common Idioms
description: Popular English idioms and their meanings (B2)

questions.text: 'It's raining cats and dogs' means:
questions.explanation: This idiom means it is raining very heavily.

questions.text: 'Break the ice' means:
options: to start a conversation in an awkward situation
questions.explanation: 'Break the ice' means to do or say something to relieve tension in an awkward situation.

questions.text: 'Hit the nail on the head' means:
questions.explanation: To 'hit the nail on the head' means to describe exactly what is causing a situation.

questions.text: 'Under the weather' means:
questions.explanation: Feeling 'under the weather' means feeling slightly unwell.

questions.text: 'Bite off more than you can chew' means:
options: taking on more than you can handle
questions.explanation: This idiom means you have taken on a task that is too big for you to manage.

questions.text: What does 'ambiguous' mean?
options: open to more than one interpretation
questions.explanation: 'Ambiguous' means something that can be understood in more than one way.

questions.text: Choose the correct word: The speech was ___ — it inspired the entire audience.
questions.explanation: 'Eloquent' means fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing.

questions.text: What does 'meticulous' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' describes someone who is very careful and precise about details.

questions.text: 'Inevitable' means:
questions.explanation: 'Inevitable' means it is impossible to avoid or prevent.

questions.text: Which word means 'to make something happen sooner'?
questions.explanation: 'Accelerate' means to increase speed or cause something to happen faster.
